s2386: Where the arrows cross, who has to give way?
s2387: According to paragraph 12 of Article 32 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, if the paths of vehicles cross and the order of passage is not determined, the driver must give way to the vehicle approaching from the right. According to paragraph 2.3 of Chapter 2 of Annex 1 to the same Law, road sign 2.3 "Give way" marks a road on which the driver must give way to drivers on the road being crossed, and according to subparagraph "a" of the note to the same Chapter, signs 2.3 and 2.4 apply to the intersection of carriageways in front of which the sign is placed.

s2391: In what order should the vehicles moving in the direction of the arrows drive through the intersection, if the emergency service vehicle has its flashing blue special light and siren switched on?
s2392: According to subparagraphs "a", "b" and "c" of paragraph 4 of Article 36 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, at an uncontrolled intersection: a) at an intersection of roads of unequal importance, the driver of a vehicle on the secondary road must give way to vehicles approaching on the main road, regardless of the direction in which they will continue; b) if the main road changes direction at the intersection, drivers on that road must follow the rules for intersections of roads of equal importance among themselves; drivers on the secondary road must also follow these rules among themselves; c) at an intersection of roads of equal importance, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles approaching from the right. According to paragraph 2 of Article 51 of the same Law, when an emergency or special service vehicle approaches with its flashing blue special light and siren switched on and/or giving signals through a loudspeaker, road users must make way on the carriageway for it, and for any vehicle it is escorting with dipped headlights on, and stop if necessary.

s2407: According to paragraph 1 of Article 35 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when passing oncoming traffic, the driver must leave enough free space to the side and, if necessary, keep close to the right edge of the carriageway. If movement on their side is made difficult by an obstacle or other road users, they must slow down and, if necessary, stop to let the oncoming vehicle or vehicles pass. According to paragraphs 2.3 and 2.5 of Annex 1 to the same Law: road sign 2.3 "Give way" marks a road on which the driver must give way to drivers on the road being crossed, and, where plate 8.13 is present, to drivers on the main road. Outside built-up areas, sign 2.3 is also placed in advance, 150–300 m before the intersection, with plate 8.1.1 if sign 2.3 is placed in front of the intersection, or with plate 8.1.2 if sign 2.4 is placed in front of the intersection. Road sign 2.5 "Priority to oncoming traffic" prohibits the driver from entering a narrow section of road if this would hinder traffic coming the other way. The driver must give way to an oncoming vehicle that is on the narrow section or at its opposite approach.
